matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert every Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value, sum the terms on each side of the equality, and compute the difference between the two sides. This numeric gap tells you how much the total must increase or decrease to achieve a valid equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: For "VII = XVIII - VI", LHS = 7, RHS = 18 − 6 = 12, discrepancy = 7 − 12 = −5.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each character present in the equation, respecting stick orientation. Include the numeric change each transformation would cause.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the set of possible value changes that a single‑stick addition or removal could produce.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure that both the character you removed the stick from and the character you added the stick to remain valid Roman numerals or operators. An invalid shape (e.g., a single diagonal) disqualifies the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For every candidate stick relocation, check the resulting symbols before accepting the move.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X to make V is valid; removing a diagonal from V would leave a single diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick can be moved from a V to make an X (value +5) or removed from an X to make a V (value −5). The orientation of the stick stays diagonal, and both resulting symbols are valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the discrepancy is a multiple of 5 and a V or X appears in the equation, consider moving a diagonal between them.
matchstick.example: Changing V → X in "VI" turns it into "XI" (+5); simultaneously changing X → V in "XVIII" reduces that term by 5.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical stick from II yields I (value −1). The same applies to longer vertical stacks (II ↔ III, etc.) as long as the resulting numeral remains standard.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is ±1 (or a multiple of 1) and an I or II is present, consider adding or removing a vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Turning I into II in "VII" changes the value from 7 to 8 (+1).

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus sign (−). Conversely, adding a vertical stick to a minus sign creates a plus sign. This changes the sign of the adjacent term.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the discrepancy can be resolved by flipping the sign of a term and a vertical stick is available to move.
matchstick.example: Changing “– VI” to “+ VI” adds twice the value of VI to the RHS.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: A stick retains its original orientation when moved; a diagonal stick cannot become vertical or horizontal, and vice versa. Transformations must use sticks of the same orientation as the target shape requires.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the search for a valid move, enforce that the orientation of each moved stick matches the orientation needed in the destination character.
matchstick.example: A diagonal stick taken from X cannot be used to extend an I, because I requires a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of all numerals and the overall equation to verify whether equality holds. Do not rely on visual intuition alone.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any proposed transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning VI into XI, recalculate RHS: 18 − 11 = 7, which matches LHS = 7.

matchstick.title: Match discrepancy with possible value changes
matchstick.principle: Prioritize transformations whose net numeric effect (increase or decrease on the appropriate side of the equation) equals the computed discrepancy. Discard moves whose net effect cannot bridge the gap.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After enumerating possible single‑stick changes, filter them by comparing their signed net change to the discrepancy.
matchstick.example: For a discrepancy of −5, a V→X (+5) on the RHS matches the needed change, while a V→X on the LHS would not.

matchstick.title: Paired stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Moving a stick from one character to another is equivalent to a removal transformation on the source and an addition transformation on the destination; compute the numeric change for each side and sum them (taking the sign of the side) to obtain the net effect on the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a single‑stick move involves two different characters (e.g., taking a diagonal from X and adding it to V). Use this to evaluate whether the combined effect matches the discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X (10 → 5, −5) to V (5 → 10, +5) on the same side yields net 0; moving it from X on the RHS to V on the LHS yields net +10, which could resolve a discrepancy of +10.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets that stick orientation is fixed and conflates diagonal and vertical sticks when visualizing transformations.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the stick being moved; a diagonal can only become part of another diagonal‑based symbol, never a vertical I.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick without verifying that the remaining strokes still form a legal Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a stick, immediately validate that the source symbol is still a recognized numeral/operator before proceeding.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver focuses on numeral changes and overlooks that flipping a minus to a plus (or vice versa) can change the equation’s balance.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When the discrepancy cannot be matched by numeral changes alone, consider converting ‘–’ to ‘+’ by moving a vertical stick, and recompute the arithmetic.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes the visual modification automatically yields a correct equation and does not recompute numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick relocation, recalculate the integer values of all terms and check the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Assuming the equality sign cannot be altered
matchstick.why_it_happens: The solver treats ‘=’ as immutable, missing solutions that involve moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to another symbol while preserving an equality elsewhere.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat ‘=’ like any other operator: a horizontal stick can be moved away only if another horizontal stick is added back to keep a valid equality sign.
